Niles Valentine has kept his wife, Matilda, in the dark since the start of the 2026 TV schedule about his plan to move to Ghana. He finally decided to drop the bombshell in this latest episode, and predictably, she was pretty upset to learn he was no longer working toward bringing her to the United States. Given her anger, there was a possibility this married 90 Day couple could split at the end of the season.

With various rumors floating around the internet about their status, I decided to do a bit of digging to see what I could find on whether series veterans Niles and Matilda are still together. While I didn't expect either of them to break their contract agreements and explicitly say one way or another, I think it's safe to say it looks like they're still together, with some predictable updates.

Niles posted a photo on Instagram of what appeared to be the inside of an apartment in the United States back on November 13th. Readers can take a look at the post below, in which he showed the difference someone's posture can make. Take a look:

A post shared by Niles Valentine (@roman_cupid_95)

That doesn't look like any room in Matilda's apartment, which has me guessing he's back in the United States at this point. I can't claim to be an expert on apartments in Africa, but I've lived in a good deal of American ones that have that exact same look when it comes to the bathroom!

Niles returning home feels like the most obvious outcome in this season of 90 Day Fiancé: The Other Way. Matilda married him in the hopes of coming to the United States and not just having a better life for herself but for her family back in Africa as well. She's obviously mad that Niles couldn't make it happen as soon as he promised, but that doesn't mean she wants him to give up.

If Niles has returned to the US, I think it's fair to speculate that he and Matilda are still together. The pair still follow each other on Instagram, which usually feels like an obvious sign that 90 Day couples are still together and married.

Why 90 Day Fiancé's New Florida Spinoff Has Me Questioning If We've Lost The Plot

If we get to the end of 90 Day Fiancé: The Other Way and learn that Niles is still working to bring Matilda to the United States, I won't be surprised. That's been the goal from the start, and I think he made a rash decision to move to Africa without looking into how difficult it would be for him to start a life in the country.

Niles may not be incredibly wealthy, but his earning potential in the United States is likely higher than it would be in Ghana. Even if she doesn't have her husband with her, I can understand wanting to wait as long as it takes for him to find a way to bring her to the United States rather than changing the plan.

90 Day Fiancé: The Other Way continues on TLC on Sundays at 8:00 p.m. ET. We'll see how things shake out for Niles and Matilda down the stretch, and keep an eye on the other couples taking part as well.

#3718. Blade Runner 2099 bosses hint at a possible "triple-A" Blade Runner game in the future - just don't expect it any time soon

Blade Runner 2099 - an upcoming TV miniseries coming to Amazon Prime Video, acting as a sequel to Blade Runner (1982) and Blade Runner 2049 (2017) - might be getting a video game. And a 'triple-A' video game, at that. At least that's according to Andrew Kosove and Broderick Johnson, executive producers for Blade Runner 2099 and co-CEOs of Alcon Entertainment (which owns the Blade Runner IP).

In a new interview with IGN, the duo reveal that they had thought about adapting the Blade Runner fracnhise into a game, and that - should it come to fruition - it would target "triple-A" in scope. Other than that, the duo seemed to want to keep any potential information to themselves. Given they appear to be in talks about the title, rather than in any active development, if something did come of this ideation, it would no doubt be a long, long way off. Kosove and Johnson's aim seems to be getting players to "interact" more with the world of Blade Runner, which has recently been fleshed out by the 2017 movie and is set to be developed more in the upcoming series.

Of course, we've seen Blade Runner games before. There was 1997's simply-titled Blade Runner - developed by Westwood Studios and published by Virgin Interactive - which was a point-and-click adventure that really seemed to pick up the vibes the original Ridley Scott was putting down. An Enhanced Edition of the game was released in 2022, which is actually more of a remake than a simple enhancement.

Then, in 2023, Annapurna Interactive unveiled its very first internally-developed game, in the form of Blade Runner 2033: Labyrinth. The game, which promised to riff on the dystopian universe established in Ridley Scott's cult classic movie, would have been sandwiched squarely between that film and its sequel, Blade Runner 2049. It was going to be set in LA after the Blackout hits, but beyond that - and the fact it's coming to PC and consoles at some point - few details ever managed to break through the PR barrier before the game went dark: it's been removed from Annapurna's website and delisted from Steam. Curious.

If you want to see something more from the cyberpunk world sooner, Blade Runner 2099 releases on Prime Video on 25th November.

Grand Theft Auto 6 is on a rolling launch, which means everyone's getting access at different times.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

GTA 6 launches at midnight on November 19 in your own local time zone for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S according to Rockstar support. Since it isn't a simultaneous global launch time that does mean that folks over in New Zealand (and everyone else in the same time zone) will be the first to play GTA 6. More on that below.

Since there's no time zone conversion to do in this case, I'll break down the info in a way that may be more useful to you. Here's how far behind your time zone is from New Zealand's. This is how many hours behind the first GTA 6 players booting up the game you will be in your area. I feel like everyone in Florida should get an upgrade from ET to NZ time in this one case, just sayin'.

Okay, this is decades old console lore stuff. As explained above, a rolling launch that happens at midnight local time means that people in New Zealand will unlock GTA 6 first. For big launches of years past, some folks have changed the region setting on their console to spoof being in a different time zone. That means they can unlock the ability to start playing the game before midnight in the time zone where they're actually located, get it?

Is the New Zealand trick going to work for GTA 6? I'm not sure, I only know that people will definitely try it. Some launches of years past have put measures in place to block the trick. Here's Sony's guidance on changing your PlayStation account region versus Microsoft's explainer on updating your Xbox account country, which you shouldn't do unless you're actually moving to New Zealand this month, of course. Don't tell Rockstar you heard anything from me.

All the cloak and dagger stuff is sort of thrilling, maybe, but I'd take a global launch as is standard on PC any day.

#3716. Eight 'Winter Arc' Rules That Will Actually Deliver Results

There are a lot of terrible social media trends out there aimed at self-improvement, yet even though everybody has been making fun of the "Winter Arc" craze, I actually think it’s a good one. During your Winter Arc, you promise yourself you’ll stick to your fitness and self-care routines during (and despite) the end-of-year chaos. It's a good goal, with one caveat: Make sure you choose rules that will actually improve your life and deliver results.

Think of the “arc” in the sense of a “story arc.” The Winter Arc is a self-improvement journey that unfolds over the last few months of the calendar year. The most hardcore #gymtok-ers will tell you the Winter Arc officially begins on Oct. 1, but others start in early November, or whenever they get around to it. The "when" isn't critical, though—whenever you read this is a fine time to start. The close of the Winter Arc is fixed, however: It ends Jan. 1, just as everybody who is less dedicated than you is waking from their holiday food comas and resolving to get in shape.

You get to choose your own terms for your Winter Arc. The general vibe is one of locking in, committing to your goals, and actually doing the things you’re always saying you’ll do. TikToker @carlyupgraded has said that her own mental image of someone nailing their Winter Arc is “hood up, headphones on, getting ready to go for a run in the rain at 5 a.m.”

It turns out I’ve accidentally been Winter-Arc-ing for years; I just didn’t know it had a catchy name. Why save your gym routine for New Year’s when you’ll have the place to yourself all December? We’re even gifted with an extra hour in the mornings to fill with something productive.

I really love the mindset shift involved. Commonly, people are active in the summer (great time for outdoor fun), may or may not stick with their routines in the fall, and let everything fall apart as the holidays approach. Who has time to go to the gym when you’re planning Thanksgiving, attending holiday parties, studying for final exams, or whatever else the end of the year throws in front of you?

But that’s the exact reason why this time of year is the best to start (or restart) a fitness routine, or really any kind of routine. When you start a routine during a busy time of year, you’ll be forced to make it sustainable. The gym routine you can stick with amid the chaos isn’t going to be one you drop after a few months. You’re already training yourself to work around obstacles as they come up, which is a key component of self-efficacy. And when the chaos clears on Jan. 1, your routine will be even easier to stick to.

Of course, there are ways to lean in too hard: Choosing unsustainable habits, falling for bad diet advice, mistaking not masturbating for some kind of health hack, the usual suspects. There’s also the pitfall of focusing too much on the vibes and too little on what you’re actually going to do or how you’ll benefit.

And then there’s the framing: You were working on yourself all year, but you’re in danger of letting up on the gas, but you’re committed to locking in so that you’re a step ahead of everybody who takes this time to slack off. I really don’t love this tack. Self-improvement is not a competition. There’s a difference between being consistent in your training and healthy eating (good) and seeing the pursuit of health and fitness as something where you always have to work harder because you’re at risk of getting left behind.

I also don’t love how gendered the Winter Arc TikToks tend to be. When you search for Winter Arc content, the first few suggestions include “winter arc for women” and “winter arc for men.” When I first started looking at the Winter Arc trend a few years ago, the women’s versions were more likely to include restrictive dieting or to focus on how the Winter Arc will finally (sigh) snatch your waist. These days, the focus is more on personal goal setting: Lots of the girlies filming their Winter Arc rules are doing so in a notebook and talking about journaling exercises that will help you identify what you need to work on to get to your "best self." Sometimes this is all monetized; training plans and journaling prompts can, of course, be purchased at the link in bio.

I do like that many of the women’s versions emphasize sustainability and setting your own goals rather than copying somebody else's. I don't love the enormity of the mental burden you're supposed to shoulder before even beginning. Should I really have to file an in-depth written report with myself before revamping every area of my life with a 100% commitment to multiple goals?

The men’s versions tend to go off the rails in another direction, with rules like “no girls” or “go ghost.” No distractions! Here, I've seen a shift over the years as well: at first there was overly serious content, followed quickly by satire (yelling at the viewer to get divorced and go work out in the dark). Now the men's videos tend to be more vibes-based, featuring images of pre-dawn workouts and plates full of salad with motivational quotes playing in the background. When the men give their rules, they tend to be simpler than the women's—no journaling exercises—but they often boil down to the same overly strict routines. (And then, of course, they'll offer to sell you a 90-day or 60-day plan.)

If you’re going to do a Winter Arc (or if you’re already doing one), make sure to structure it in a way that benefits you. Choosing 10 overly ambitious goals and setting yourself up for failure is not a healthy way to approach self-improvement, OK? Pick goals that are meaningful, achievable without divine intervention, and trackable with tools you already have at hand (for example, tracking your steps with a Fitbit or your running mileage with a Garmin watch).

It’s also helpful to think of developing yourself over this arc, rather than taking it as a three-month (or two-month) challenge where you have to do everything right all the time. If you currently wake up at 8 a.m. and want to wake up at 5 a.m., you don’t have to set your alarm for 5 a.m. tomorrow. It’s OK to aim for 7:30 a.m., make that a habit, then try for 7:00 a.m., and so on.

With that in mind, here are some "rules" I've seen from creators that I'm actually on board with (so long as you don't overwhelm yourself with them):

Wake up earlier. A great goal, especially if you take advantage of the time change to make things easier on your body.

Get to bed on time. Never a bad idea. Cultivating good sleep habits in general is always worthwhile.

Get your steps in. Be thoughtful about what your target is: 10,000 is not for everybody. Better to choose a number that would be a modest improvement on what you already do.

Exercise X times per week. Pick a number that works for you, and get into it. Be realistic about your goal, and for the best results, be consistent even if you’re sore at first.

Eat healthy. This is a great goal, with the major caveat that there are a lot of ways to eat healthy. You don’t need to cut out sugar or pretend that there’s something evil about seed oils. Do get more protein and veggies.

Be more thoughtful about using social media. I’m not going to tell you to delete all your apps (“except TikTok,” as the TikTokers say). But it’s fair to consider whether you might want to delete a few apps, turn off some notifications, or put your phone on Do Not Disturb for more hours of the day.

Journal or read more. Journaling can be great for working through your feelings or cultivating a creative habit. Reading can be entertainment or a great way to learn. Choose whichever you need most.

Learn a new skill. I’ve mostly seen this one in the men’s TikToks, and I love it. They’re often thinking of “skills” that will help in some kind of entrepreneurship grift they’re about to sell you, but there are tons of skills that will come in handy in life, or that are at least fun to learn. Practice a language, get better at cooking, make some art. Skills are, as I’ve noted, a multi-layered exercise for your brain. And they may come in handy someday.

This year I've slacked off on my fitness routine as I've gotten more involved in other hobbies, but I'm actually looking forward to being more consistent. My winter goals include exercising early in the day when possible and reading 20 minutes each day. (I'm even tracking the second one with a sticker chart.)

#3715. There’s One Thing I’ll Admit The Ocarina Of Time Remake Made Worse

I wrapped up the Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake this weekend, and overall enjoyed it a lot. It was refreshing to go back to the old puzzle-driven style of Zelda after a decade of the sprawling open world of Breath of the Wild. Though thereâs been some debate within the community about whether or not Nintendo made the game too easy, I didnât really pay that much mind. In fact, only one thing in the remake really struck me as a downgrade: the updated version of one of my favorite songs in the gameâs stellar soundtrack.

The Spirit Temple is typically the last major dungeon Link fights his way through in Ocarina of Time before the endgame, and itâs in the dangerous deserts of Hyrule where the player hasnât stepped foot until now. Thereâs an air of mystery to everything youâre doing in this segment of the game, but also precariousness, as youâre in what youâve been taught up to this point is enemy territory. This is the land of the Gerudo, where Ganondorf, the embodiment of evil, was born and raised. So when you arrive here, youâre already on edge, expecting to find some kind of malevolence buried beneath the sand.Â

The music has to capture that feeling of uncertainty, trepidation, and danger, right? The evocative power of the original Spirit Temple track blaring through my CRT TV when I played Ocarina of Time is still a core memory of this game for me. The MIDI instrumentation is unlike anything else in the game, with its use of big, booming gongs, synth strings and, perhaps most importantly, what sounds like a duduk that plays the somewhat dissonant melody. Much of this remains intact in the remake, but the mix is far more ambient, with the melody blending in with the string arrangement, instead of being elevated and piercing through the soundscape.

Itâs certainly more chill, and while the composition is still lovely, the mix just doesnât hit as hard. When I played through the Spirit Temple in the remake, the song quickly became background noise, rather than something that was constantly needling away at my nerves like in the original. Thankfully, I can boot up the 1998 game at any time, but I hope newcomers who never played the original can still get that same feeling of uncertainty and ethereal awe from the remake that I felt when I first walked into the Spirit Temple all those years ago.

#3714. Treyarch lays off lead Call of Duty writer and Zombies veteran after "approximately 20 years" of service

"Thanks to all the fans for your enthusiasm, support, and kind words over the years."

Treyarch's former Senior lead writer, Craig Houston, has been laid off after approximately 20 years of service with the developer. In a post made to both his Twitter/X account and LinkedIn, the developer thanked fans for their support during his two decades with the company and confirmed he was impacted by recent reorganistation within the studio.

"After approximately 20 years, I was sadly one of those affected by recent layoffs," he noted in his posts. "I am proud to have worked with so many talented people - many of whom will remain friends for life. Thanks to all the fans for your enthusiasm, support, and kind words over the years."

On Twitter/X, he quote tweeted a video celebrating 30 years of Treyarch and featuring footage from many of the games he worked on to share his message. It appears the layoffs referenced are part of the broad reorganistation affecting 3200 jobs that Xbox announced earlier this year. Treyarch, as part of Activision Blizzard, is owned by Xbox.

Houston is a bonafide veteran of the esteemed FPS series. His first Call of Duty title at Treyarch was Call of Duty 3, where he worked as a video editor. This was followed by World at War, Black Ops 1 through 4, where he is credited as a writer and designer. For Modern Warfare, Black Ops - Cold War, Vanguard, Modern Warfare 3, then Black Ops 6 and 7, he is listed as a member of the design team and in 'creative development'. He is not credited on this year's Modern Warfare 4.

If you've picked up a Call of Duty game in the past decade-plus, you'll have interacted with Houston's work: he was a central creative force behind the writing for Treyarch's campaign modes since 2006 (with Call of Duty 3) and the main writer for the Zombies mode since 2008 (with Call of Duty: World at War). Alongside Jimmy Zielinski, Jason Blundell, and Kevin Drew, Houston was an integral part of the evolution of the Zombies pillar of Call of Duty, and shaped it into the series-defining thing it is today. There has been a fair amount of community support for Houston since he announced the news yesterday; he was a popular dev, and a lot of the Zombies-specific fan communities online hold a lot of respect for him.

"Craig is a great guy," notes one user on Reddit. "You can tell how much he loves the story/characters he writes just by how excited he is when he talks about them in promo material."

"You're a Legend Craig, it was an honor to work with you," says ex-Treyarch vet, Tony Flame, in a reply to Houston's X post. "You created a truly special experience that will live on in the kinds of millions fans. Wishing you the best [...]."

From all of us here at Eurogamer, and myself personally - who really admires the character-work and emergent storytelling present in the Xbox 360-era Call of Duty games, specifically - we wish you the best and good luck with the future, Craig.

With the 2026 TV schedule heading into the holiday season, many are likely preparing for their favorite yuletide programming and getting ready for other festivities. We can reportedly count Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce amongst such people, as they are reportedly figuring out their first Christmas as a married couple. And apparently, deciding where to spend the holiday has become a little complicated. Per a new report, the newlyweds want to celebrate with both families without making either set of parents feel left out.

The Grammy winner and her Kansas City Chiefs tight end husband on married July 3 at Madison Square Garden, an event Kelce later described as one of the best nights of his life. Now, Rob Shuter alleges in his Naughty But Nice substack that the newlyweds have been discussing their first Christmas together. Per Shuter, an insider claims:

Neither wants to disappoint their parents, but they also don’t want their first Christmas as a married couple to become a tug-of-war. They want everyone to feel included.

It's a familiar holiday scheduling problem, although the families involved are rather more recognizable than most. Swift's parents, Andrea and Scott, have long been central to her Christmas celebrations, while Kelce remains close to his mother, Donna, and father, Ed. Swift even grew up on a Christmas tree farm in Pennsylvania, an experience she later turned into a holiday song. With both sets of traditions to consider, choosing where to spend the holiday allegedly hasn't been straightforward.

The Kelces already have some well-established food traditions. Kylie Kelce has praised Swift's baking alongside Donna Kelce's famous dinner rolls, so there would apparently be no shortage of people willing to contribute to Christmas dinner.

Also, the couple may already have a solution in mind. Instead of traveling between family gatherings or deciding which parents to visit, Shuter's sources says Swift and Kelce are considering hosting Christmas themselves. The idea would bring their relatives to one celebration, although no final plans have been publicly announced. A second source told Shuter:

They think bringing everyone together is the perfect answer. They get to start their own traditions without making either family feel they’ve lost out. It’s about creating one big family Christmas.

There's at least one reason a gathering away from a football stadium might be easier this year. As it so happens, the Chiefs don't have a game scheduled on Christmas Day in 2026, according to the team's published schedule. Kansas City is set to host the New England Patriots on Dec. 21 and the San Francisco 49ers on Dec. 27, leaving Christmas Day free of a game-day obligation.

Last Christmas looked a little different for the couple. The Chiefs played the Denver Broncos at Arrowhead Stadium on Dec. 25, with Swift and her parents in attendance. She and Kelce also surprised several stadium employees with Christmas gifts.

Kelce has already talked about looking forward to his first Christmas as a married man. Earlier this month, while promoting Tommy Hilfiger's winter collection, he told Women's Wear Daily he was excited to start new traditions with Swift. Although there's at least one he's apparently keeping: his mom Donna's homemade blueberry muffins.

The families have spent Christmas together before. Back in 2023, the “Shake it Off” performer's brother Austin showed up at a Chiefs game dressed as Santa Claus and surprised Kelce with a Christmas present. Both families also played a part in the couple's July wedding, with Austin serving as Swift's man of honor and Jason Kelce standing beside his brother as best man. The newlyweds even asked guests to make charitable donations instead of bringing wedding gifts. So, getting everyone together for Christmas wouldn't exactly be a first for the newlyweds.

Neither Swift nor Kelce has confirmed Shuter's report, so where they'll spend Christmas and whether both families will be there remains to be seen. But with the holiday just a few weeks away, they still have time to figure things out. However they end up celebrating, might I suggest checking out our list of the best Christmas movies? At least that'll give everyone something to watch once the presents are opened.

Amazon has dropped the price of the two-pack Netgear Orbi 770 Series Wi-Fi 7 Mesh System to $449.99 from $549.99, saving you $100 on a setup that includes a router and a satellite node, with a combined coverage area of up to 5,500 square feet. If you don't need quite as much coverage, smaller configurations, including a single satellite node, is also discounted as part of Amazon's early Black Friday sale. It now costs $239.99, down from $349.99, and covers up to 2,750 square feet.

The system uses tri-band Wi-Fi 7 technology to spread your connection across three bands, with combined speeds of up to 11,000Mbps. It also supports wider 320MHz channels, though you'll need compatible Wi-Fi 7 devices to take advantage of those faster connections. If you prefer wired connections for devices that need a more stable link, the main router has three 2.5GbE LAN ports and a 2.5GbE WAN port, while the satellite offers two 2.5GbE LAN ports. This gives you plenty of room to connect a gaming console, desktop PC, or smart TV, and you can also use wired backhaul if your home has Ethernet cabling.

Once everything is connected, you can handle setup and day-to-day management through Netgear's Orbi app, while a web dashboard offers additional settings (for anyone who wants more control over their network), including VPN access and port forwarding, notes this PCMag review. There's no USB connectivity or 10GbE support, and some of its more advanced security and parental control features require a separate subscription after a free 30-day trial. #3710. Cyberpunk 2077 mod Torrent adds 3D rain, lightning storms, and tyre spray to Night City

A new Cyberpunk 2077 mod has overhauled Night City's rain, swapping the game's flat wet weather effects for individual 3D drops and adding lightning storms.

As spotted by DSOGaming, modder CyanideX's mod, Torrent, gives each raindrop its own size and falling speed. The drops also react to the player's movement, so they stream towards the windscreen when you're driving fast. If you find the wind has picked up, blustery weather can also push them sideways, too.

The rain also catches the light from street lamps, neon signs, car headlights, and taillights, and won't fall through roofs or inside buildings. Drops splash on the ground, heavy rain leaves mist in the distance, and cars throw up spray from their tyres on wet roads.

The mod complements this with a new lightning system, with branching bolts that flash and flicker before fading, and that can arrive in bursts during heavier storms.

If you like a little lightning, the frequency of bolts can be adjusted across 10 levels, and with the AudioXL mod installed, thunder follows each strike, timed to how far away it landed.

For players sensitive to flashing lights, a Reduce Flashes option dims the lightning, replaces its flicker with a single slow glow, and halves the number of strikes.

Torrent supports Nova City 2 and other weather mods, and adds extra storm effects for Nova City 2 players, including mist that rolls through the streets with the wind. It’s available now on Nexus Mods.

If you own a Steam Frame and want to use your Steam Controller at the same time (perhaps even playing 2D games on a big virtual screen), you've likely had to use the passthrough, or just really know your controller. That's because, despite Valve noting that the Infrared LED in the controller makes it trackable in the Steam Frame, it has not yet implemented said tracking. However, a modder has once again come to PC gamers' rescue.

Taking to the Steam Frame subreddit, user Kalluts has shared their Controller Utils GitHub project, saying, "Valve still has not released their official tracking support for the Steam Controller, so I had to take the matters into my own hands."

Effectively, their script turns on the controller's built-in IR LED, using the Frame's tracking services to pick it up. From here, it displays a 3D model of the controller in VR, and it even has a few animations.

The Steam Controller does not work like a traditional VR controller, though one user says, "I just wanted to know if I could attempt to play Beat Saber with it if I stole a second one from my friend. I know it's stupid, but I needed to know." It turns out you can't (and with just the one LED, its tracking wouldn't be good enough for a fun time anyway).

If you're wondering why one might want to use the Steam Controller in VR if it doesn't work like a VR controller, VR headsets can also run flat games on a virtual monitor.

In the right environment, a VR headset makes playing a game feel like you've just jammed a huge TV in your room. Kallut's implementation does have the ability to control the Steam VR UI, though, which is a nice touch. It also works even if you've got a skin on the controller, as the IR shines through the regular status LED on the controller.

As of right now, this Steam Controller tracking support only works in Valve's Stable and Beta SteamOS channels, and the Preview channel has not yet been tested. Kalluts also points out that the one LED makes tracking inconsistent, so if tracking starts to drift, "just hold the controller in front of you again and it should recover eventually."

Kalluts goes on to clarify that "since this interfaces directly with the native tracking, if Valve pushes some updates to those components the tracking might break. But I'll try to maintain this at least until Valve releases official tracking support for the Steam Controller."

We don't yet have a timeline on when Valve plans to implement its own tracking, but this is a pretty good workaround until then.

#3708. Your Android Can Get Hacked Without You Doing Anything at All

You probably know that clicking suspicious links online or opening attachments from strangers in an email or text is a recipe for hacking. It's a dangerous world out there online, so it's always important to be vigilant. However, the danger doesn't always involve something you do. There are ways to hack your devices without requiring any intervention on your part whatsoever—and one such example is likely plaguing your Android device right now.

As reported by The Hacker News, there is a critical Android security flaw that could enable remote code execution on your device. In other words, bad actors could use the flaw to run their own code on your phone, effectively taking over the device for their own gain. The flaw, identified as CVE-2026-58868, isn't universal, but it is widespread: It currently affects Android 14 through Android 17, the latest version of Google's OS. If your phone runs Android 12 or Android 13, it may be unaffected, as Google doesn't identify these versions in its security bulletin, but it doesn't explicitly rule them out, either.

There are two silver linings here, however. One, Google hasn't confirmed any active exploits for this security flaw. While that isn't a guarantee that bad actors have missed this exploit so far, it at least opens that possibility. As such, there may be time for users to patch their devices before hackers truly take advantage of the flaw. Second, Google does have a patch for the flaw. The patch may not be available to you right away, however, as it's up to both the manufacturer of your phone and your carrier to issue these updates. Still, a patch is, at the very least, on its way.

This flaw is perhaps the most important to fix, but it's not the only serious issue. In all, Google's latest bulletin highlights 216 vulnerabilities, and, of those, 23 are "critical." As The Hacker News explains, two other of those critical flaws could also allow remote code execution when exploited.

To see whether the patch is installed on your end, open the Settings app on your phone, tap "About phone" or "About tablet," then choose the Android version on-screen. Look for a date of "2026-11-01" or later. All security patches from Nov. 1 and on will fix this issue. If not, you'll ned to wait for the patch.

Mormon Wives: Orange County doesn’t exactly live up to its name.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

If you’ve ever watched The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives, you know there’s no shortage of drama. Just look at Taylor Frankie Paul, who’s had a swingers scandal, the cancellation of her season of The Bachelorette, custody issues with her children, and chaos surrounding production. But the Hulu reality series was popular and created a lot of buzz, so I was not surprised when they announced the spinoff, The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives: Orange County, currently on the 2026 TV schedule. However, the fact that it feels like the majority of the women in the new show are not Mormon and that some aren’t even wives is a bit weird and an interesting choice, considering the title, and viewers (including myself) have taken notice.

To catch you up in case you haven’t seen the original series, Jen Affleck, a 20-something Mormon wife and mother, joined MomTok in Utah to fight against the typical social norms and stereotypes that are common within the religion. After appearing in Season 34 of Dancing with the Stars as a celebrity contestant alongside fellow Mormon Wives star Whitney Leavitt, the mother of three with a fourth on the way decided to stay in Southern California, citing the fracturing of MomTok and the need for therapy to recover from everything that happened.

Seeming to instead have decided to jump right into another reality series, which again is an interesting choice, Jen has brought together a new group of friends, all of whom are mothers with their own drama and secrets, but who are not all Mormon, despite the show’s name. One has even admitted to signing on for the heightened visibility reality TV brings.

It’s hard not to notice that The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives: Orange County is a cast divided into two groups, with the women who are Mormons being outnumbered by the women who are not. In the season premiere, cast member Aspyn Ovard (who's got a memorable storyline about being part of a throuple) says, “We’ve all been shaped by Mormonism in one way or another,” which is a bit of a vague statement when we don’t know all the details of the backgrounds of many of these women, and even she makes it clear that she’s very closed off to the church and its teachings.

I'm not the only one who has noticed this either, as this conversation has popped up all over social media, including places like Reddit, where fans have asked why non-Mormons are "even on the show." I get it's weird to call out someone's religious preferences, but when your show is called Secret Lives of Mormon Wives, I do think that leads to a certain expectation.

When you’re in the business of entertainment, building a franchise off of something successful and popular makes sense. But it’s hard to escape the weirdness of not really delivering on what your show’s title promises. All of this is not to say that the women who make up the OC spinoff cast don’t have compelling lives of their own, because they do, but the religious branding doesn’t entirely fit and feels like more of a subplot than a main focus, like it is in the original series.

And it all makes me wonder if the title should have just been something more reflective of Jen Affleck specifically? Just spitballing here.

For a reality show that’s supposed to be centered around Mormons, The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives: Orange County actually positions them to be the villains of the season. McCall DaPron, the older sister of the OG series’ Mayci Neeley, exhibits confrontational behavior. She gets into frequent clashes with other cast members, often leaving them to wonder whether it’s possible to keep this friend group together.

Her strong commitment to her faith and her efforts to share it with others, including best friend and co-star Jordan McClanahan (whom she successfully converted), rubs anyone not as devoted the wrong way. This is especially true when her need to influence others’ opinions and actions creates conflict.

The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives has had a seemingly endless amount of drama and scandals over four seasons, which are streaming with a Hulu subscription, but Mayci always came across like the most supportive one of the group on that show, where McCall seems less inclined to stay neutral. It’s hard to know how much of the drama is manipulated with editing, but it’s another interesting choice on a series that already seems to be trying to break its own formula.

All of this said, if there ends up being a second season of the OC spinoff, I will still definitely be tuning in!

Between Jen being pregnant with her fourth child at the same time she decides she wants a divorce, Aspyn trying to get her ex-husband to spend time with her current throuple, and Salomé Andrea figuring out if she can reconcile with a man she began dating in ninth grade and couldn’t marry in the Mormon church before she ultimately walked away from both, it is all definitely weird, but just weird enough to make me want to see what happens next.

#3704. 'Ocarina of Time' for Switch 2 Might Already Have a Weird Glitch

Thursday is a big day for Zelda fans. That's when the remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time officially launches on Switch 2, marking the first major linear (i.e., non-open-world) 3D Zelda game since the 2016 Twilight Princess remake on Wii U. I, for one, have been waiting for this day for years. I loved the N64 original and the 3DS remake, so to have the chance to play a modern take on the definitive Zelda is so exciting—that is, if it actually runs as it should.

I stumbled upon this interesting post on X from Austin John Plays, a YouTuber with a host of Zelda coverage. According to Austin John Plays, Ocarina of Time already ships with a weird glitch that won't necessarily break your experience, but which may slow it down for a while, and perhaps even confuse players into thinking something is wrong with their game or their console.

As his post explains, if you're playing the physical copy of Ocarina of Time, and it's the first game you've ever played on your Switch 2—maybe you got one of those fancy new Zelda anniversary consoles and want to break it in properly?—you may run into glaring performance issues: The game may freeze, your controller may stop working, and the FPS may drop to single digits.

Luckily, Austin John Plays says the fix is easy: just wait. Eventually, your game will boot back to the title screen. When it does, don't try to play right away. Instead, close the game, restart your Switch 2, then try relaunching Ocarina of Time. Austin John Plays advises you may need to repeat this process two or three times, but after that, you shouldn't continue to run into issues. I wouldn't be surprised if Nintendo releases a patch right away for this glitch if it turns out to be as widespread as this post implies.

However, seeing as the game doesn't come out until tomorrow, there's something you can do to prevent it. Austin John Plays thinks the bug only impacts Switch 2 consoles that haven't run other games before. If you've had your console a while, you're likely set. But if you just bought the 40th anniversary Zelda edition of the Switch 2, you might not have had a chance to run a game on it yet. As such, download a game from the e-shop—even a free demo—just to get the system running. Hopefully, that will be enough to circumvent the glitch, and prevent issues when Ocarina of Time launches tomorrow.

#3703. EA hires another former Call of Duty boss to take the lead on all Battlefield Studios' projects

EA has made some notable leadership changes within its studios group, and in who oversees the Battlefield franchise. Byron Beede, previously Battlefield's general manager, has been promoted to group general manager.

Beede announced the change on LinkedIn, saying that he now oversees EA's shooter and action-RPG portfolio, seemingly occupying the role of the late Vince Zampella.

In this stead, EA appointed Sam Cooper as Battlefield's new boss. Cooper, who also revealed his new job title on LinkedIn, previously had a stint at EA Sports, but he's mostly known for his work at Activision, where he spent the last five-ish years as Call of Duty's global product management and head of live service.

While this might seem like fairly unremarkable corporate news - executives move between rival companies all the time, after all - it reinforces a narrative that EA continues to keenly replicate Activision's Call of Duty model.

That particular push is years-old now, and it kicked off in 2021 when EA hired Byron Beede, former boss of all of Call of Duty at Activision, to lead the next evolution of Battlefield. So far, that decision has given us the very successful Battlefield 6 and its free-to-play, COD: Warzone-like battle royale mode Redsec.

To facilitate that, EA rearranged several of its studios to serve under one banner dubbed Battlefield Studios, replicating Activision's model of locking several teams around the world into developing and supporting a single game / franchise. Ripple Effect, Motive, the iconic Criterion and, of course, series creator DICE are all the Battlefield franchise's lead and support studios.

Many players argue - and I would agree - that Battlefield and Call of Duty games are more alike today than they've ever been. The user interface, the emphasis on limited-time events, the garish store cosmetics, the COD-like battle pass system - complete with a more expensive option, are all signs of that transition. And that is to say nothing of controversial changes to longstanding Battlefield tenets, such as the class system, intended to make Battlefield 6 appeal to a wider audience.

The effects of that leadership change likely won't materialise until the next Battlefield title, but it's a curious one to keep in mind as EA leans even harder into its biggest franchises following its $55bn private equity and Saudi Arabia's PIF-funded buyout.

Working to a deadline is hard enough, but working towards one that can be moved if you really need it is worse. Grand Theft Auto 6 has been in the works for around a decade, including a couple of delays so devs could polish up some rough edges, and after all this time it must be really hard to step back and say enough is enough.

"They would never stop working on this game if they had the choice," Jennifer Kolbe, head of publishing, says in an interview with The Guardian.

We now know that part of the reason why GTA 6 was delayed was because of the sheer amount of NPCs that needed kitting out with dialogue and audio. Talking to Bloomberg co-head of Rockstar North, Rob Nelson, explained how the delay wasn't strictly necessary but not delaying would have meant GTA 6 "won't be the game we want to make."

Nelson expands on this with The Guardian: "It’s really hard to close it down. If you step away and get a little bit of space from it, you can look at it objectively and go: 'I'm proud of what we’ve done'. But ultimately, it is being taken away from you, and you do the best you can to finish it in the time that you’re told."

“They could have made GTA 5.5, and done it faster,” Kolbe adds. “Ultimately, that’s not what they wanted.” No, instead the devs were hellbent on creating something new, expansive, and an aviary for a few dozen bird species.

"What we have grappled with is the transition from being limited by technical constraints to being limited by human resource constraints," Nelson says. "Like, how much can we physically build? You can keep going forever … People say you can throw money at the problem, and you can to an extent, but it’s no guarantee of making something good."

"You have to take big swings. It can’t be just more of the same."

#3700. Umamusume: Pretty Derby parent company plans to release seven new games by 2030 as it boasts an "88 percent hit rate" on its mobile titles

Cyberagent - the parent company of Umamusume: Pretty Derby developer Cygames - has boasted its recent successes in the mobile gaming sphere in a recent quarterly earnings presentation.

As part of this presentation (covered by Automaton), the company has established plans to launch seven "major releases" to the mobile platform by 2030. There is no word on what these games will be, but one will be released in 2027, while another two will come in 2028.

Cyberagent boasted an 88 percent "hit" rate for its mobile releases so far, with seven of its eight releases having a development budget of around a billion yen, and reaching a point where it makes that figure back every month from its playerbases. Those games include Umamusume: Pretty Derby, Final Fantasy Ever Crisis, Hololive Dreams, and Jujutsu Kaisen Phantom Parade.

CyberAgent CEO Takahiro Yamauchi - speaking during the presentation - noted that it was still difficult to predict the success of a mobile game ahead of its release. However, he also claims that the experience Cyberagent has gained with its big releases to date have allowed the company to gain a clearer perspective on profitability and sustainability.

This presentation comes after a notable month for Cygmes and Umamusume: Pretty Derby. The developer issued refunds for hotels and flights following the sudden cancellation of an LA live show for the game last month, then shortly after became a major sponsor of the Japanese Formula 1 Grand Prix. The game was also temporarily taken offline due to the major PHP vulnerability exposed last month, an outage that was thankfully short-lived.

#3699. 10 Shows Like 'Phony' You Should Watch Next

You can find him on Bluesky.

This is Streamalikes, where you can find a curated list of recommendations to stream based on what you already like.

What if you knew your mom wasn't really your mom, but no one believed you? That's the improbable but entertaining premise of Hulu's Phony, which stars Sam Nivola as a teenager who wakes up from a car accident and quickly comes to believe that his mother (Friday Night Lights' Connie Britton) is an imposter. Of course, no one believes him. I'm not sure I believe him, but it'll be pretty boring if it turns out that he just had a really bad concussion the whole time.

It's a coming-of-age drama and a surreal mystery with hints of comedy, and though it borrows elements from other shows, it stands apart for the skill with which it blends everything together. While you wait to see how the story plays out, here are 10 more twisted mysteries to stream now.

A twisty-turny (and well-reviewed) bit of fake identity folderol, Apple Cider Vinegar stars Kaitlyn Dever as Belle Gibson, a real-life Australian cancer survivor (except not really!) With a cheeky sense of humor and a willingness to distort reality, the show follows the wellness influencer as she fakes multiple cancer diagnoses in order to better market her alternative, MAHA-esque app and remedies to the unwitting. As her livelihood comes under threat, her lies grow more elaborate. Stream Apple Cider Vinegar on Netflix.

Alia Shawkat stars here as Dory Sief, an aimless millennial who decides, after seeing a missing-person poster for a college acquaintance, that she's going to make it her purpose to track her down—with the extremely begrudging support of her friends. But neither Chantal nor her disappearance are anything like what Dory expects. The show shifts focus from season to season. Initially a darkly comic take on a Nancy Drew-style mystery, it later finds the gang desperate to cover up a mostly unintentional murder, and getting in deeper each season. It's a funny, smart, and weird and shares talent with Phony in the form of writer/producer Anthony King, who serves as co-showrunner on the new series. Stream Search Party on Netflix.

This one's largely about adults, so it skips the coming-of-age angle central to Phony, but it has a quirky mystery, gaslighting, and a protagonist whose sanity is questioned by just about everyone all the same. This fun and very loose adaptation of the 1989 Tom Hanks film finds Keke Palmer's Samira and Jack Whitehall's Rob moving back to his impossibly safe and tidy hometown. Their house happens to be across the street from a dilapidated Victorian eyesore that may or may not have been the location of a murder a couple of decades before—a murder of a girl who made the mistake of trying to get away. As Samira adjusts to new motherhood and life on the cul-de-sac, she learns that even the nicest of her neighbors have secrets, and comes to suspect that her husband knows more about the missing girl than he's letting on. Stream The 'Burbs on Peacock.

When pretty, popular girl Kate Wallis (Olivia Holt) goes missing without a trace in 1993, awkward Jeanette Turner (Chiara Aurelia) steps in to fill the gap, modeling herself after Kate, working her way into the missing girl's social circle, and getting close with her boyfriend. That's all going great until Kate reappears two years later, accusing Jeanette of having witnessed the events around her disappearance and keeping quiet. Whoops. There's even more going on, as the show shifts back and forth between 1993, 1994, and 1995 to slowly reveal the missing pieces. Stream Cruel Summer on Hulu.

Based on a Harlan Coben novel, Fool Me Once is a bit more of a political thriller than a coming-of-age thing, but we're still in "what the hell is up with my family?" territory: Michelle Keegan plays Maya Stern, a former special ops pilot dealing with the murder of her husband, whom she then impossibly catches playing with their daughter on a nanny cam. The resulting mystery ties into the earlier death of her sister and leads to a web of conspiracy involving her husband's family and a shady pharmaceutical company. Stream Fool Me Once on Netflix.

A vibe match more than anything else, this dark and twisty mystery with a slightly surreal sense of humor also features a single mom who is definitely not what she appears to be. Kim Mo-mi (Lee Han-byeol, initially), the Mask Girl of the title, is a uniquely complicated woman; she always wanted to be a K-Pop idol, but it was always made clear to her that she's not nearly pretty enough for that kind of stardom. So, in order to fill that void, she's got a side hustle. On top of her boring office job, she puts on a blonde wig and a mask to perform as a camgirl for anonymous men. It's a means to express herself creatively and sexually with a level of control—until a mistake causes her to lose that control, a co-worker discovers her secret life, and desperation leads to murder. The show shifts perspectives continually, feeling most like Phony when it focuses on Mo-mi's daughter. Stream Mask Girl on Netflix.

Flipping things around a bit, albeit in a similar "am I just being paranoid?" vein, The Girlfriend deals with a mom who may or may not be freaking out for no reason. Starring Robin Wright as Laura Sanderson, a wealthy art gallery owner in London whose son (Laurie Davidson) brings home a new, working-class girlfriend, Cherry Laine (Olivia Cooke)—immediately strikes Laura as not-our-kind. But is there more to it? Can someone with the name "Cherry Laine" truly be trusted? There's definitely something off, and we're kept guessing as to whether or not this is the story of a dangerous con artist or an overbearing mom—or maybe a little of each. Stream The Girlfriend on Prime Video.

Coming from Irish playwright and Derry Girls creator Lisa McGee, this show eschews the relatively subtle dark comedy of Phony for something much more gloriously surreal. Three high school friends from Belfast reunite after learning that an estranged bestie has died unexpectedly—except that maybe she didn't; a mixed blessing given that they all have secrets that they were hoping would be buried with the maybe departed. Now they're off to investigate the mystery of the murder(?), which turns into a hunt for the friend that they only thought they knew, while inadvertently revealing plenty of secrets of their own. The tone is all over the place in a way that somehow works, with flashes of sincerity balancing out the comedy. Stream How to Get to Heaven From Belfast on Netflix.

Shin Hye-sun offers up a phenomenal performance as Sarah Kim (well: sort of), a wealthy businesswoman who is discovered, at the series' opening, under a sewer grate. The police detective charged to investigate quickly finds inconsistencies in the woman's identity, and after interviewing Sarah's friend and business associate, comes to feel that neither woman is exactly (or anything, like she seems. Though it takes itself more seriously than Phony, it's still an addictively twisty mystery built around a constructed identity. Stream The Art of Sarah on Netflix.

There's a lot going on in this steamy, telenovela-esque drama. Camila Román (Carolina Miranda) finally meets Fernando Castell (Rodolfo Salas), a Tinder match, in Las Vegas, and things get very hot very quickly—he's everything he seemed to be and then some. If anything, she's the sketchy one: a dancer, not a nurse as she said, and with a possessive ex following her around. Still, it's all going great until she decides to surprise Fernando after he flies back to Colombia (which: never do that), and gets a totally different dude when she asks for him at his work. And that's just the beginning! Stream Fake Profile on Netflix.

#3698. The next Xbox, Project Helix, is a console and "not a PC" says Microsoft, as it clarifies that computational power isn't sole focus this time

"It is about leveraging new technical advancements such as neural rendering."

Microsoft has stressed that its next-generation Xbox console, Project Helix, "is not a PC that can also play console games", but rather "a console that is also capable of playing games from your PC". The company has also underlined the importance of using gen-AI-adjacent "neural rendering" technology going forwards, and a desire to remove "all the barriers of play that have historically existed" - notably in making the past generations of games playable.

The details come from a Microsoft-produced Xbox magazine made available digitally yesterday, and a Helix-related feature speaking to Xbox vice president of next generation, Jason Ronald. "When we think about Project Helix, it's really designed to be the ultimate gaming machine," Ronald said, "one that removes all the barriers of play that have historically existed. My entire library is accessible to me. I'm able to bring four generations of my Xbox library and progression with me and have it available instantly. And we remove the arbitrary constraints between console and PC games.

"We're very clear on the design goal," Ronald later added. "Helix is designed to be a console that is also capable of playing games from your PC. It is not a PC that can also play console games. The goal is making it easy, intuitive, and instant to access my games. But if you're a hardcore gamer or a power user who wants to have that deeper level of customisability across settings and performance options, you can absolutely go do it."

Notably, Ronald seemed to suggest that Helix - the console, not the handheld; "Helix" refers to a couple of machines - isn't solely focused on computational grunt. Indeed, he said the next generation wasn't about hitting 8K resolutions and 240 hertz frame-rates, but instead leaning on technologies like "neural rendering" - i.e. generative-AI - and encouraging innovation.

"It's about deeper immersion," Ronald said. "It is about leveraging new technical advancements such as neural rendering to deliver a new level of visual fidelity in more efficient and innovative ways. It's about new kinds of games and new game experiences that we haven't been able to do before. What excites me about the future is the idea of entirely new types of games that have never been possible before, delivered through all the innovation in the silicon and the hardware and the platform that we're delivering."

While referencing the global component shortage and exorbitant prices of computer hardware, he added: "This is a big reason why we're really focused on advancements like neural rendering because it's an entirely new way to generate a frame without requiring more computational horsepower, additional memory, and things like that. I think you're going to see more innovation over the next three to five years than you've seen in the last 10 years."

Xbox boss Asha Sharma also recently talked up the importance of generative-AI-sounding technology in Xbox's future, saying "too many ideas never become games", and that "a single person will soon be able to wield capabilities that once required entire nations".

Another key part of Xbox's Helix vision is compatibility and game preservation. "Game preservation is core to Xbox," Ronald went as far as to say. "Not only do we feel like it's the right thing for the industry, we feel a deep responsibility as one of its biggest platforms and publishers. For the first 30 years of game development, nobody really thought about game preservation when they were designing their hardware, when they were building their games." Xbox is apparently working with game-makers to ensure games can not only be played now but also 20 to 30 years into the future.

The other key facet of Microsoft's push the familiar Play Anywhere mantra, whereby one game can be played across multiple devices, maintaining your game-progress as you go. This is fundamental to Microsoft's handheld-and-console Helix plan, and something we've seen the company dry-run with the Xbox ROG Ally X handheld. "It's this notion that not only does my library move with me, but my progress moves with me as well," Ronald said. "Because I fully expect that when I'm in the middle of an 80-hour RPG, if I'm 25 hours into that and I want to play it on another device, I should be able to instantly resume from where I was. Those are things that today are becoming more common, but I think in the future it's going to be a baseline expectation of all players."

Ronald wouldn't be drawn on the issue of price regarding Project Helix - a recent report suggested Helix could be priced up to $1800 - referring to it only as both "a challenging time" but an "exciting one", because "we have to invent entirely new technology to continue to advance the state-of-the-art while also continuing to make things accessible and affordable". Ronald also wouldn't reference a release date, though the report referenced above suggested the handheld Helix machine will release next holiday, 2027, and the console Helix machine the year after. The next generation, then, seems to be around the corner.

Some minor spoilers from the new NCIS season follow.

NCIS Season 24 is off to a hot start, and it's been giving a lot of screen time to Michael Weatherly's Tony DiNozzo, who is currently the new NCIS director. With that storyline dominating, there's been little time to follow other fan-favorite plotlines. This has really gotten me to thinking about how the show cooled off on a potential Jessica Knight and Nicholas Torres romance. CinemaBlend recently had the chance to speak to Knight actress Katrina Law, and I had to ask her about what's going on.

I recently had a chance to speak to Law, and after talking about the recent episode marking the first time she worked with her daughter, I had to know what's going on with Torres. I wondered if fans should just give up on Knight and Wilmer Valderrama's character having a relationship. Here's what she said:

Well, as we know in the show, especially one that's gone on to season 24, nothing's ever dead. And there's always a chance for anything to come back. that being said, I feel like there's such a fun dynamic between night and tours that kind of verges on the, the, the side of brother and sister. And with mixed with a little bit of tension in there, which just makes it kind of awkward and fun and like a little sizzly underneath

Law can't just outright spoil anything she's already filmed for the 2026 TV schedule, but it's good to hear this perspective. It seems she's fine with the current situation as it stands, which has remained professional (and only somewhat spicy) so far. As a fan, it always feels like there's a chance it could escalate into something, but both characters seem to wonder if it's worth the trouble.

I actually personally think, based on her first comment, that Law might not want Knight to have a relationship with Torres. Is it because of what she said after, and the guilt she'd feel for Brian Dietzen's Jimmy Palmer? She continued:

If we do lean into that, I feel so bad for Jimmy, because, you know, Knight in Shining Palmer, and I just feel like that's just so brutal. But you know, television, we got to get the viewers in, so who knows where we're going.

I can appreciate Katrina Law's empathy when it comes to Jimmy Palmer. Jimmy and Jessica's relationship was fun while it lasted, but it feels like the door is closed on them ever reconciling and getting back together. Hear me out: Is she just supposed to ignore Torres and the obvious chemistry just because it might hurt her ex's feelings?

Personally, I think fans would say no, and I have a feeling Jimmy would say the same. He's a mature adult, and he's gone through the ups and downs of romance. Provided Nick doesn't start some feud with him sometime ahead of time, I don't see him putting his foot down and not giving this relationship his blessing. It may make work just a little awkward, but I think he'd be able to move past it.

If not, maybe we could see Brian Dietzen's character put in for a transfer, and Jimmy would join another NCIS spinoff. He was a recent guest star on the New York spinoff, so maybe that opens the door to him joining their team at a later date? I'm sure Sam would love to have a vet like him on board, and fans would love to see Jimmy get a new place to spread his wings.

All that aside, though, we'll have to keep watching NCIS on CBS on Tuesdays at 8:00 p.m. ET to see if there's any momentum between Knight and Torres. In the meantime, there's never a shortage of crimes for the team to solve, and it's been fun to see them navigate that with Tony as their boss.

#3695. Can GTA 6 make $2 billion in its opening weekend? One industry analyst has run the numbers, and seems to think so

We all know the story of GTA 5 making more than $1 billion in the first three days it was on sale, right? At the time, Take-Two believed this to be the fastest any entertainment property had achieved the impressive milestone - music and films included. It made history, and with ease. And it looks like GTA 6 is going to do even better.

At least, that's according to one analyst, Joost van Dreunen, a senior data analyst and great writer/numbers diviner who wrote some predictions in his respected SuperJoost PlayList newsletter. "My prediction: Take-Two announces opening-weekend sales above $2 billion by Monday, 23rd November," he wrote. And you know what? I reckon he's onto something.

Let's review what we already know: there is a conservative estimate of 10 million pre-orders for Rockstar's latest game floating around - something buoyed by comments from Take-Two boss Strauss Zelnick - and, even by the company's lofty expectations, we know the game is tracking "well above expectations" when it comes to pre-orders.

We also know a lot of people are shelling out for the slightly more pricey Ultimate Edition (£90). So many people are opting for the more expensive version, in fact, that Take-Two revised its financial forecast up to $3.5bn for the next financial quarter, thanks to "recurrent consumer spending" (something Zelnick clarified in an investor's call is explicitly linked to the Ultimate Edition). 10 million pre-orders, at roughly $100 per copy - that's $1 billion right off the bat.

"That’s two days faster than its predecessor," van Dreunen said, "and largely before anyone has even played the game." That other $1bn will come over the weekend. And then, per the analyst, the game will sell roughly another 28 million copies over the course of the first year it's on sale. "My forecast puts first-year sales at 38 million copies, only modestly ahead of GTA 5’s 35 million. The real difference may be how much revenue each player generates over the years that follow."

But it's what follows in the newsletter that intrigues me most. "At the high end, [GTA 6] may just lift the entire industry with it," wrote van Dreunen. "In the face of AI slop and shitty mobile games that exist only to extract revenue, it will offer a reprieve. At a time when the industry is increasingly focused on making games cheaper and monetising players more aggressively, Rockstar is about to demonstrate the enduring appeal of spending a fortune to make something people actually want to play."

So, even if you're dubious about the game and Rockstar's motivations for selling as many copies as possible, the launch of GTA 6 could be something that gives the industry a much-needed jolt of life, in the face of rampant layoffs and shrinking talent pools.

It's not all sunshine and rainbows ahead for Rockstar, though: amongst the frenzy of launch activity, Rockstar has been embroiled in legal action after it was accused of union busting following the firing of over 30 employees. The case's conclusion will be determined this week, as the game goes on sale.

#3694. Firefox's New 'Mini Window' Feature Is a Game Changer for Productivity

David Nield is a technology journalist from Manchester in the U.K. who has been writing about gadgets and apps for more than 20 years.

He has a bachelor's degree in English Literature from Durham University, where he also spent a term as editor of the award-winning student newspaper Palatinate. His journalism career started in print media, where he contributed to and edited several technology magazines and bookazines sold in the U.K. and internationally. More recently, he has worked as a freelancer for some of the biggest technology publications on the web, covering everything from on-the-ground reporting about product launches, to detailed explainers and how-to guides on apps, gadgets, and platforms. His expertise covers broad areas of consumer tech, including smartphones, laptops, wearables, and AI.

For many of us, web browsing involves juggling dozens of tabs at once, and it's easy for important pages to get lost in the chaos. Now, Firefox has introduced something I think could help us multi-taskers: a "Mini Window." As highlighted by ZDNET's Jack Wallen, this new Firefox feature works like picture-in-picture overlays for videos—only here, that PiP displays a website.

"[Mini Window] lets you move a tab, or a selected section of a page, into a compact window that stays on top of your other windows while you browse," runs Mozilla's official blurb. "It's useful when you're multitasking and need to keep a few sources of information in view at once: Reference docs, a chat, a video call, a form you're filling out." As such, Mini Window doesn't necessarily replace running tabs side-by-side; rather, you can prioritize one tab in a full-size window, while keeping another page in view at all times.

This is a feature that's still in its early stages, and right now you can only get it in the "Nightly" version of Firefox, a very early beta version of the browser. Mozilla says it will push the feature to the full version of the browser later this month.

If you want to try this out as soon as possible, first install Firefox Nightly on your Mac or PC. Once up and running, you can launch Mini Window by right-clicking on a tab header and choosing Move Tab > Move to Mini Window. The tab shrinks and drops down to the lower right corner by default, staying on top of all other windows (not just Firefox). You can then scroll through the page and follow links as normal in the Mini Window—any links set to open in a new tab (manually or automatically) will launch in the main Firefox view, not the window overlay.

By dragging the title bar around, you can put your Mini Window anywhere you want on screen, and you can change its size by dragging the edges of the window too—so it doesn't necessarily have to be all that "mini." Firefox hides all buttons by default—including forward, backward, and refresh buttons, together with the address bar and buttons for closing the window or putting it back as a normal tab—though they appear when you hover over the Mini Window.

I'm finding the feature most useful when writing up articles where I need to refer to something else already on the web (so almost all of them), but there are a host of ways this can be used. It's particularly handy on a small laptop, where you don't necessarily have the screen space to put two tabs side by side, or when running a lower-priority window (like checking a social media site while reading an important document). No doubt, Firefox will continue to refine and improve the feature as it makes its way to the stable version of the browser, and it feels like something other browsers (looking at you, Google Chrome) might adopt as well in the near future. Eventually, using Mini Windows might become as common as opening up a long row of tabs.

A video game console exploded last month at a repair shop in Santo AndrÃ©, Brazil, injuring two of the people who worked there. Police are calling it an attempted murder, and say a rival business owner was trying to eliminate his competition. The man they think was responsible was arrested over the weekend as part of a separate investigation.

G1 Globo reports (via Dexerto) that the original incident took place on October 23 at around 5:30 p.m. A delivery person dropped off a gaming device for some sort of repair, but inside the retro gaming console, police say there was a concealed timer and two cylinders filled with flammable liquid. Investigation into Megaspeed first started in 2024.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Megaspeed is a company with a lot of eyes on it at the moment, and many eyes makes many, uh, news stories. The US Department of Commerce and Department of Justice have thought it to be a good time to drop some details on its investigations into the Singaporean datacentre company, once led by one Alice Huang.

If you've already forgotten who Alice Huang is, she was the person first suspected of having an affair with Jensen Huang. The ex-Nvidia CEO later admitted to an affair with someone that has remained unnamed.

It wasn't just the affair that sunk Huang, it was the suspicion that Alice Huang may be a Chinese Intelligence asset, according to a New York Times report. That was later rebuffed by Attorney General Todd Blanche and the CCP. It was also that the company Alice Huang ran, Megaspeed, was suspected of chip smuggling; and the other two alleged affairs thereafter with Nvidia employees.

"After identifying suspicious activity through proactive monitoring of potential sensitive semiconductor diversion, the Department of Commerce initiated an investigation into Megaspeed in 2024 for potential export control violations.In May 2025, Department of Commerce investigators requested records from Nvidia concerning direct or indirect sales to Megaspeed.In June 2025, Nvidia placed Megaspeed on its 'no sell' list. Based on the Department of Commerce’s investigation, agents from the Department’s Bureau of Industry and Security, in conjunction with Singaporean law enforcement officials, conducted an on-site, in-person, end-use check at Megaspeed in June 2025 and interviewed CEO Alice Huang."

There's a lot to chew on there. Megaspeed holds it was cleared of any suspicions of diverting chips to China in contradiction of US export rules. It claimed in a statement, dated December 23, 2025 (once the above Commerce investigation had taken place):

"We want to be absolutely clear: over the past six months, our company has undergone multiple on-site inspections and reviews by key institutions, including the Bureau of Industry and Security of the US Commerce Department, the Ministry of Investment, Trade and Industry of Malaysia, and Nvidia. These thorough investigations have confirmed that there has been no evidence of any violations concerning the illicit transfer of chips or any illegal activities, and this demonstrates that we are a compliant and legitimate company."

Nvidia also long held that Megaspeed was in the clear, with a company spokesperson saying the accusations against Megaspeed were "thoroughly investigated and debunked last year".

That's not quite the end of US investigations into the company, however, as the agencies suggest in their joint statement:

The PC Gamer Circuit Breaker newsletter breaks down the latest PC gaming tech, and finds you the best deals on the best products

"Following this enforcement action [by the Department of Commerce], the Department of Justice took the lead role in the criminal investigation of Megaspeed."

That doesn't specify that it's ongoing, but the statement begins with the two agencies noting they wouldn't usually talk about an ongoing investigation, but felt it necessary to "provide facts and address inaccurate information circulating in public reporting."

"The Department of Justice and the Department of Commerce’s Bureau of Industry and Security working together will bring the full extent of the law against Megaspeed for any criminal conduct that may have occurred. This investigation is the result of the excellent work of the Department of Commerce under Secretary Howard Lutnick and the law enforcement efforts of the Department of Justice under Attorney General Todd Blanche."

On its website, Megaspeed posted the following statement on November 12, the day Jensen Huang stepped down as Nvidia CEO. It is addressed from Tan Yong Pong, James, Chairman & CEO of Megaspeed:

"Megaspeed takes its compliance obligations under U.S. export control laws extremely seriously. Compliance is a fundamental priority for the company, and Megaspeed is committed to working constructively and transparently with the U.S. government.Megaspeed has cooperated with inspections by the U.S. Department of Commerce’s Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) and stands ready to cooperate fully with any other relevant U.S. government authority.To further reinforce our commitment to compliance, Megaspeed has retained a leading U.S. law firm to lead a comprehensive census of its graphics processing units (GPUs) and independently verify its export control compliance practices.Megaspeed welcomes appropriate government scrutiny and is committed to demonstrating through concrete actions that it operates responsibly, transparently, and in accordance with applicable U.S. laws."

Megaspeed also said that Alice Huang officially left Megaspeed on August 30, 2025 and has no role with the company.

Singapore has agreed to continue discussions with the US about Megaspeed, which just goes to show how intently the United States is looking into this whole chip affair. The country has also tightened export controls to curb China's access to Nvidia GPUs remotely, as this has been suggested as one way many Chinese models may have been trained on cutting-edge Blackwell GPUs they should not be able to purchase otherwise.

#3691. Ever wanted to play a multiplayer version of Cyberpunk 2077 with your friends? Well, thanks to a mod now in beta, you can

You may have recently read that CD Projekt Red's in-development Cyberpunk 2 may be trying to revive the original game's online ambitions. But, if you don't want to wait the many years it'll likely be before the Cyberpunk 2077 sequel arrives, then I've got good news for you: Cyberpunk 2077 multiplayer mod CyberMP is now out in open beta.

"After almost six years of development, countless reworks, and code rewrites, we're finally launching the public beta," the modders on the CyberMP Discord channel wrote (thanks RPS). "Anyone can jump in and play now - no invites or applications needed." The team notes, however, that this is "true beta", meaning "Crashes, desyncs, and server drops under heavy load are completely normal for now. That's exactly why we need testers."

Alongside the potential shakiness, the devs say it's also possible the mod could ping your anti-virus software, since it "doesn't have a digital signature yet". Whilst the priorities for the team lie in "polishing the foundations" and "fixing crashes and stability", more features are eventually planned. But for now, they stress, "let's see how the project handles real player traffic!"

So, what exactly is it? CyberMP is a dedicated multiplayer modification for Cyberpunk 2077 that allows you and your friends to explore Night City together: drive vehicles, engage in combat, and play custom community-created game modes on high-tick dedicated servers. You need an official copy of the game to play it (obviously), and the mod is completely free to download. You can download the mod, and read a fair amount of how to get it working, what to expect from it, and how to troubleshoot any issues, over at its dedicated website.

If you're thinking 'Hang on, why does Cyberpunk 2077 multiplayer sound so familiar?', it's because the game was supposed to receive an official multiplayer mode after its original release. Thanks to its shaky launch, however, plans changed, and CD Projekt Red later announced that multiplayer would be a separate "triple-A release", but, eventually, that too was cancelled. The studio is still keen to honour the idea, though, and recently stated it's "focusing on bringing online into all of our franchises one day".

This isn't the first big bit of news we've had about Cyberpunk 2077 mods this week. Just yesterday, a new mod called 'Torrent' added 3D rain, lightning storms, and tyre spray to Night City - all rendered and made lovely with a new lighting system that seems to play nicely with other weather mods that have been created for the game.
